quote: Injections were performed as local infiltrations. ... This is injected in subcutaneous tissue around the flap base, pedicle, and inset margins.
proposed_wording: Intradermal injection appears nowhere — neither permitted nor prohibited by the label the page read, and never studied with the marketed product: in dermatologic surgery Exparel has been given by local infiltration of the surgical site, into subcutaneous tissue (Rames 2026, PMID 41603645), and volunteers received it subcutaneously (Apseloff 2013, PMID 23458225); the only human intradermal liposomal bupivacaine data come from an unmarketed academic formulation (Grant 2004, PMID 15220782).
reason: Answer to the question: no — the full text never uses 'intradermal' or 'dermal'; all liposomal bupivacaine was given as 'local infiltrations' (PDF p. 4) of 'the surgical site and surrounding skin' (p. 1), and the only tissue plane the paper names is subcutaneous (around flap base, pedicle and inset margins for linear closures and flaps; saline-diluted wide-field infiltration with no plane named for large hidradenitis wounds). It was injected after the procedure, separately from the initial lidocaine or buffered lidocaine (not mixed in the syringe), was not used for nerve blocks, and across 136 administrations in 127 patients the only recorded adverse event was nausea in 2 patients taking opioids, with no CNS or cardiovascular events and no LAST. The paper matches the marketed product and human population but not the intradermal route, so the claim stays confirmed; two PubMed searches for this paper (counts 4 and 23) found no human intradermal study of the marketed product — the nearest are Grant 2004 (unmarketed formulation), a dog RCT of the veterinary liposomal suspension infiltrated partly into the intradermal layer (Hixon 2023, PMID 38241783; animal, veterinary product) and Apseloff 2013, whose abstract says subcutaneous although PubMed's MeSH lists 'Injections, Intradermal'. Not reached: the route in two Mohs letters (Chang 2022, Yadlapati 2021) and a dermatologic-surgery review (Sorenson 2019), which have no abstract and no free full text; the label clause was not re-checked (Rames cites a 2023 label revision only for nerve-block indications).
